text:
Maria: Heads-up — after the `runtime/kernel-selector` merge onto canary we see a p99 token latency jump (~45%) on kv-heavy customer traces. Canary id: canary-42. Noticing it only on longer sequences + high kv hit ratio.
Jon: Oof. Which merge exactly? PR/commit?
Maria: The merge was 2 days ago, commit a1b2c3d -> merged to release branch. Small heuristic change: prefer kernel X for medium sequence lengths. Logs: `kernel_selector::choose_kernel` spend spiking. Flamer: http://perf.local/flame/189345 (internal).
Pranav: I can run git bisect locally on my devbox if someone posts a repro harness. Is there a perf test that triggers KV/cache + batching?
Maria: Yes — use `perf/benchmarks/kv_batch_replay.sh` with dataset `kv_traces/sample_long.json`. Command: `./kv_batch_replay.sh --seq-len 1024 --batch-size 48 --reps 200`. That reproduces p99 locally for me.
Sasha: Quick question — does this repro when KV cache disabled? just to isolate kernel vs cache.
Maria: Good call. With `--kv-cache-off` it's fine (p99 back to baseline). With cache ON and hit ratio > 0.6 we see the regression.
ci-bot: CI job 7623 (canary-smoke/latency) failed p99 threshold. See https://ci.redwood/7623.
Jon: OK that narrows it: kernel selector + KV caching interaction. Possible path: kernel X assumes no KV streaming or had different loop ordering, causing extra mem copies when KV present. Can someone run `perf record` and a short `perf script` around `choose_kernel`?
Pranav: On it. Running `perf record -e cycles:u -p $PID -- sleep 30` now against local repro. Will paste flame excerpts.
Pranav: (paste) `choose_kernel` top callers: `select_for_batch`, `kv_prefetcher::apply`. Hotspot shows a memcpy-like op in fallback path.
Maria: I also see increased syscalls: `madvise`/`mmap` churn when cache hits are high. Could be new kernel path allocating temp buffers for KV mapping.
Sasha: Candidate suspects: (1) fallback kernel with safe copy; (2) batch-size heuristics changed threshold causing more fallback; (3) subtle prefetch ordering change.
Jon: Can we bisect quickly? Proposed steps: 1) create a minimal git range from release branch between commit before merge and the merge; 2) run `git bisect run ./perf/ci_bisect_runner.sh --workload kv_batch_replay`; 3) use pass/fail threshold p99 > baseline+20% = bad.
Maria: I'll kick off the bisect on a beefy machine (A100) to match canary infra. Running `git bisect start && git bisect bad a1b2c3d && git bisect good z9y8x7w && git bisect run ./perf/ci_bisect_runner.sh` now.
deploy-bot: Started bisect on builder-12. Estimated 7 steps. Logs: https://ci.redwood/bisect/189345.
Pranav: While bisect runs, I reproduced locally and added extra logging in `kernel_selector` to dump chosen kernel name + kv_hit_ratio per request. Sample output: `kernel=KX_fast fallback=false kv_hit=0.72 batch=48` vs `kernel=KX_slow fallback=true kv_hit=0.82 batch=48` — fallback path costly.
Kai: I ran a microbenchmark: KX_slow has an extra memcpy of ~0.6ms per token at 1024 seq when KV mapping present. When batch_size >= 32 and kv_hit>0.6, aggregate p99 rises a lot.
Jon: Sounds like the selector is picking KX_slow erroneously when it should pick KX_fast for this workload. Maybe a threshold inversion. If bisect points to the kerneI heuristic commit, we should revert or fix selection conditions for KV-enabled paths.
Maria: Bisect progress: step 3/7 -> candidate commit 7f6e5d4 introduces `prefer_prefetch_kernel` flag. Bisect output (snippet):
```
7f6e5d4 is bad
first bad commit: [7f6e5d4] runtime: prefer prefetch kernel for medium sequences
```
Jon: That aligns. 7f6e5d4 changed selection order. Who authored it?
Maria: @Sasha authored it in PR #1287. Sasha, can you chime in on intent?
Sasha: I suggested favoring prefetch kernel for cold-starts to reduce latency on short bursts. Looks like the patch didn't account for KV mapping case. We can patch: only prefer prefetch if `kv_enabled==false` OR `kv_hit_ratio < 0.4`.
Pranav: Quick local patch + rerun: modifying `kernel_selector::choose` guard fixes p99 in my run. I put a prototype diff in my fork.
Maria: Good fix. Two options: (A) revert 7f6e5d4 on canary to unblock rollout, (B) backport the guard fix as a small PR and hotfix canary. Which preferred?
Jon: For safety, revert the change on canary so we restore baseline quickly, then follow with the guarded reintroduce as a safer PR. Revert PR is faster.
Kai: Agreed. I can open revert PR and target canary branch. Also add a test to perf harness that runs kv-heavy traces so this doesn't slip again.
deploy-bot: Created PR #1302 to revert commit 7f6e5d4 onto canary. CI triggered.
ci-bot: CI job 7630 for revert PR running.
Maria: After revert deploy to canary-42 (rolling), p99 back to baseline on my checks. Will monitor for 1 hour then proceed with canary ramp.
Jon: Nice work. Action items: Kai to file revert PR (done), Sasha to open guarded reintroduce PR with kv guard + perf test, Pranav to add perf harness test to CI, Maria to monitor canary metrics and confirm.
Sasha: I'll open the guarded PR and include microbench numbers + rationale.
Pranav: I'll add automated kv_batch_replay to perf CI with threshold check.
Maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: Closing this thread once canary stable.
Kai: FYI added regression label + postmortem template JIRA.
Maria: Closing — moving to follow-up thread for the guarded reintroduce.
